questions.stem: Why do atoms form chemical bonds?

options.text: To increase the number of electrons they have
To achieve a stable electron configuration, usually a full outer shell

questions.explanation: Atoms form bonds to achieve a stable electron configuration, typically a full outer shell like the noble gases. This can be done by transferring electrons (ionic bonding), sharing electrons (covalent bonding), or delocalising electrons (metallic bonding). The number of protons (atomic number) never changes in chemical reactions.

questions.stem: Sodium (Group 1) reacts with chlorine (Group 7). What type of bonding forms and why?

options.text: Covalent bonding, because both elements share electrons
Metallic bonding, because sodium is a metal
Ionic bonding, because sodium transfers its outer electron to chlorine
No bond forms because metals and non-metals do not react

questions.explanation: Sodium (a metal) has 1 electron in its outer shell, and chlorine (a non-metal) needs 1 electron to complete its outer shell. Sodium transfers its outer electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. This electron transfer between a metal and non-metal produces ionic bonding.

questions.stem: Which type of bonding involves the sharing of pairs of electrons between non-metal atoms?
questions.explanation: Covalent bonding involves sharing pairs of electrons between two non-metal atoms. Each atom contributes one electron to each shared pair. Ionic bonding involves electron transfer between metals and non-metals. Metallic bonding involves delocalised electrons shared between metal atoms.

questions.stem: An element in Group 2 reacts with an element in Group 6. How many electrons will the Group 2 element transfer to each Group 6 atom?
questions.explanation: A Group 2 element has 2 electrons in its outer shell, which it loses to form a 2+ ion. A Group 6 element needs 2 electrons to fill its outer shell. So the Group 2 atom transfers its 2 outer electrons. For example, magnesium (Group 2) transfers 2 electrons to oxygen (Group 6) to form MgO.

questions.stem: Which substance is most likely to have metallic bonding?
questions.explanation: Iron is a metal consisting of only metal atoms, so it has metallic bonding. In metallic bonding, metal atoms lose their outer electrons to form a 'sea' of delocalised electrons that hold the positive metal ions together. NaCl has ionic bonding (metal + non-metal), and H₂O and CO₂ have covalent bonding (non-metal + non-metal).
